Steps.sectionTitle: Nobody should need a masking tutorial to make one photo out of two.
Steps.sectionSubtitle: The old way: an hour of pen tool, soft edges, and shadow painting. Here, it's the same work, described in one sentence.
Steps.step1Body: Drag in two to four photos — portraits, products, scenes. The first sets the lighting and camera angle of the result. JPG, PNG, WebP formats up to 12 MB each.
Steps.step2Body: A single sentence is enough. Pick a preset to write most of the prompt automatically, or write your own: who goes where, which light wins, what must not change.
Steps.step3Body: About ten seconds later, a single image arrives: harmonized lighting, consistent shadows, preserved faces. Download in high-resolution PNG.

Presets.sectionTitle: One tool, nine jobs it does well.
Presets.sectionSubtitle: Each preset is a hand-written instruction, refined over time. Pick the one that matches your need and the prompt is already written.
Presets.pageSubtitle: Each preset is a hand-written instruction. Pick the one that matches your need and the prompt is already written — all that's left is to specify what matters.

two-people.title: Two people, one photo
two-people.description: Recompose two portraits into a single frame — matched lighting, shared shadows, consistent depth of field.
two-people.prompt: Place the person from image 1 next to the one from image 2, both facing the camera. Keep exactly the faces. Match the soft evening light from image 2 and add a cast shadow under each.

swap-bg.title: Swap the background
swap-bg.description: Image one is the subject, image two is the new location. Edges, spill light, and reflections are handled automatically.
swap-bg.prompt: Keep the subject of image 1 intact and place it in the scene of image 2. Adapt the lighting, reflections, and ambient color so it looks like it was always there.

product-scene.title: Product in a real scene
product-scene.description: Drop a product on a white background into a styled environment without losing packaging detail or logos.
product-scene.prompt: Place the product from image 1 in the scene of image 2, resting on the visible surface. Keep packaging labels and text intact. Add a contact shadow consistent with the ambient light.

borrow-style.title: Borrow a style
borrow-style.description: Use the second image as a visual reference — palette, grain, contrast — and leave your subject untouched.
borrow-style.prompt: Apply the visual style of image 2 (palette, grain, contrast, light treatment) to image 1 without modifying the subject or composition.

try-outfit.title: Try an outfit
try-outfit.description: Fit a garment to the pose and body of the person, keeping the fabric texture and pattern alignment honest.
try-outfit.prompt: Dress the person from image 1 in the garment from image 2. Adapt the cut, folds, and fabric shadows to the posture. Keep the face and hands as they are.

restyle-room.title: Restyle a room
restyle-room.description: Keep your space's architecture and bring in the furniture and atmosphere from a second photo.
restyle-room.prompt: Restyle the room from image 1 with the furniture, palette, and atmosphere of image 2. Keep the existing architecture, windows, and openings. Keep proportions realistic.

logo-mockup.title: Logo on mockup
logo-mockup.description: Apply a flat visual onto fabric, a curve, or a fold so it looks printed rather than pasted.
logo-mockup.prompt: Apply the logo from image 2 onto the visible surface of image 1 (fabric, packaging, object). Curve the artwork to the surface's folds and perspective. Keep the logo's colors and contrast.

restore-combine.title: Restore and combine
restore-combine.description: Repair scratches and fading on scanned photos, then bring the subjects together in one clean frame.
restore-combine.prompt: Restore the quality of the source images (remove scratches, noise, and discoloration). Then bring the subjects together into a single consistent frame, like a cleaned-up archive photo.

holiday-card.title: Holiday card
holiday-card.description: Merge people from several photos into a warm seasonal setting that looks like a real photograph.
holiday-card.prompt: Bring the people from the source images together in a warm seasonal setting (soft lights, festive atmosphere). Keep faces recognizable. Avoid the digital-collage look.

Features.sectionTitleHighlight: putting two images side by side.
Features.sectionSubtitle: It was making the second one look like it had always been there. Here are the six things we spend our engineering time on, ordered by what breaks other tools.
Features.pageTitle: Six things we spend our time getting right
Features.pageSubtitle: The hard part was never putting two images side by side. It was making the second one look like it had always been there. Here are the six technical pillars of Fusionia.

faces.title: Faces stay faces
faces.description: We trained the model to preserve the identity of people, not to generate a new one that "kind of looks alike." Your subjects stay recognizable, even after the merge.

shadows.title: Shadows consistent with the light
shadows.description: A failed merge shows in the shadows: they point the wrong way, or don't respond to the light source. Here they're computed from the main image's lighting.

labels.title: Labels and logos survive
labels.description: For e-commerce and branding, warped text ruins the image. We keep packaging, labels, and typography crisp, at the right perspective.

ratio.title: Formats that go somewhere
ratio.description: Square, portrait, landscape, stories: you pick the output ratio at the source, and the image is composed for that frame — not cropped after the fact.

fast.title: Fast enough to iterate
fast.description: About ten seconds per image, enough to test three lighting variations before picking one. No time to grab a coffee between tries.

private.title: Your photos stay yours
private.description: Source images are deleted shortly after the merge. We never use them to train our models, and you can request their full erasure at any time.

Audience.sectionSubtitle: Different trades, the same underlying problem: two images that need to become one, without the afternoon of masking that goes with it.

ecommerce.title: E-commerce teams
ecommerce.description: One clean packshot becomes twenty lifestyle visuals without booking a studio or a set.

families.title: Families and friends
families.description: Bring everyone into a single photo, even when no one was in the same room — or the same country.

designers.title: Designers and agencies
designers.description: Mockups, key visuals, and pitches delivered in the time it used to take just to open the brief.

estate.title: Real estate and interiors
estate.description: Furnish an empty room from a reference photo and keep the architecture exactly as it is.

Faq.sectionTitle: The questions we get asked before signing.
Faq.pageTitle: Everything you want to know before signing up
Faq.pageSubtitle: The questions we get asked most often. If you can't find your answer, write to us directly.

1.question: How do I merge two photos into one?
1.answer: Import your images on the home page, pick a preset or write a sentence describing the expected result, then click "Merge." You can configure everything without an account; the final image is generated as soon as you have an active plan or credits, and comes back in about ten seconds.

2.question: Will the faces look like the real people?
2.answer: Yes. The model is trained to preserve the identity of subjects, not to invent a face that "kind of looks alike." You get a merge where every person stays recognizable, even in close-up.

3.question: What image formats and sizes can I import?
3.answer: JPG, PNG, and WebP, up to 12 MB per file. The first image determines the lighting and camera angle of the result, so choose it accordingly.

4.question: Do I need to know how to use Photoshop?
4.answer: No. If you can write a sentence, you can use Fusionia. Presets write the bulk of the prompt for you; all that's left is to specify what matters: who goes where, which light wins, what must not change.

5.question: Can I use the results commercially?
5.answer: Yes. The generated images belong to you and can be used for commercial materials, provided the source images you import are yours or you have the rights to them.

6.question: What happens to my uploads?
6.answer: Source images are deleted shortly after the merge. They are never used to train our models, and you can request their full erasure at any time.

7.question: How much does a merge cost?
7.answer: One merge = one credit. On the Pro subscription, 100 credits per month are included. Without a subscription, standalone credits are available from €0.40 per merge.

8.question: Can I cancel anytime?
8.answer: Yes, with no fees or notice. The subscription stays active until the end of the paid period, then stops. Credits already purchased remain available.
